formulas.name: Motional e.m.f.
formulas.formula: The e.m.f. generated in the circuit by the moving rod is the product of magnetic-field strength, rod length and velocity. This equation is valid when B, ℓ and v are mutually perpendicular. Otherwise, their mutually perpendicular components are used. Motional e.m.f. is an example of dynamically induced e.m.f. because it is induced in a conductor in motion.

formulas.name: Power dissipated by motional e.m.f.
formulas.formula: The power dissipated is P = B²ℓ²v²/R ...(14.2). In satisfying the principle of conservation of energy, the produced and dissipated powers are equal.

sourceReferences.sourcePdf: Books/12th/12th Physics/PDF/Physics Book for 12 class KPTBB.pdf

formulas.name: Self-inductance from flux linkage
formulas.formula: The unit of inductance is the henry (H). From Eq. (1), an induced e.m.f. of 1 V for a current-change rate of 1 A s⁻¹ gives L = 1 H. Faraday’s law also gives ε = Δ(NΦ)/Δt (2). Comparing (1) and (2), LI = NΦ, so L = NΦ/I (14.3).

formulas.name: Instantaneous alternating e.m.f. of a rotating coil
formulas.formula: The induced e.m.f. is ε = −ΔΦ/Δt = −Δ(NAB cos ωt)/Δt. Taking the limit as Δt→0 gives ε = NAB(ω sin ωt) (14.5). Since sin ωt has maximum value 1, εmax = NABω; therefore ε = εmax sin ωt = εmax sin(2πft) (14.6).

formulas.name: Motor terminal voltage and back e.m.f.
formulas.formula: The back e.m.f. ε is less than the applied voltage V. Their difference drives current through the armature resistance: V = ε + IₐRₐ (14.7), where Rₐ is armature-circuit resistance and Iₐ is current. The textbook calls the motor output the difference between supply voltage and back e.m.f.

workedExamples.question: At what rate must a single conductor cut the flux so that a current of 1.2 mA flows through it when a 10 Ω resistor is connected across its ends?

workedExamples.title: Example 14.2 — average induced e.m.f.
workedExamples.question: A coil of mean area 500 cm² and 1000 turns is held perpendicular to a uniform 0.4 gauss field and turned through 180° in 1/10 s. Find the average induced e.m.f.
workedExamples.solution: EXAMPLE 14.2 — GIVEN: When the plane of the coil is perpendicular to the field, θ = 0°. When the coil is turned through 180°, θ = 180°. Initial flux linked with the coil: Φ₁ = NBA cos θ = NBA. Flux linked when turned through 180°: Φ₂ = −NBA. Change in flux: ΔΦ = Φ₂ − Φ₁ = (−NBA) − (NBA) = −2NBA. N = 1000; B = 0.4 G = 0.4 × 10⁻⁴ T; A = 500 × 10⁻⁴ m²; Δt = 0.1 s. REQUIRED — induced e.m.f. ε = ? SOLUTION — Average induced e.m.f., ε = |ΔΦ|/Δt = 2NBA/Δt. ε = [2 × 1000 × (0.4 × 10⁻⁴) × 500 × 10⁻⁴]/0.1 = 0.04 V.

workedExamples.title: Example 14.3 — motional e.m.f., current and power
workedExamples.question: EXAMPLE 14.3 — A loop of resistance 0.1 Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 2 T. A conductor of length 0.2 m slides along a loop at velocity 0.2 m s⁻¹. Find (a) the e.m.f. produced if the conductor’s motion is perpendicular to the field, (b) the current through the loop, (c) the electrical power generated, and (d) the input mechanical power.
workedExamples.solution: SOLUTION (a) — Motional e.m.f. ε = vBℓ = 0.2 × 2 × 0.2 = 0.08 V. (b) Current through the loop is I = ε/R = 0.08 V/0.1 Ω = 0.8 A. (c) Electrical power generated is P₁ = IV = 0.8 A × 0.08 V = 0.064 W. The magnetic force on the current-carrying loop of length ℓ is F = B I ℓ = 2 T × 0.8 A × 0.2 m = 0.32 N. (d) The power needed to move the loop against magnetic force F is P₂ = Fv = 0.32 N × 0.2 m s⁻¹ = 0.064 W.

workedExamples.title: Example 14.4 — A.C. motor peak quantities
workedExamples.question: EXAMPLE 14.4 SOLUTION — Peak back e.m.f.: ε = V − IₐRₐ = 120 − (5 × 4) = 100 V. Peak power supplied: Ppeak = VI = 120 × 5 = 600 W. Peak rate of energy loss as heat: Pheat = I²R = (5)² × 4 = 100 W.
workedExamples.solution: EXAMPLE 14.4 SOLUTION — Peak back e.m.f.: ε = V − IₐRₐ = 120 − (5 × 4) = 100 V. Peak power supplied: Ppeak = VI = 120 × 5 = 600 W. Peak rate of energy loss as heat: Pheat = I²R = (5)² × 4 = 100 W.

exercises.title: Multiple-choice questions 1–14 and conceptual questions 1–8
exercises.questions:
UNIT 14 EXERCISE — MULTIPLE-CHOICE QUESTIONS (choose the best possible answer). 1. For inducing e.m.f. in a coil the basic requirement is: (A) flux should link the coil; (B) change in flux should link the coil; (C) coil should form a closed loop; (D) both (B) and (C) are true. 2. A single-turn coil rotates in a uniform magnetic field at uniform speed; induced e.m.f. is: (A) alternating; (B) steady; (C) pulsating; (D) zero. 3. Dynamically induced e.m.f. is used in: (A) choke; (B) transformer; (C) generator; (D) thermocouple. 4. In Fleming’s left-hand rule the thumb represents: (A) current flow; (B) induced e.m.f.; (C) magnetic field; (D) mechanical force. 5. The field at any point on the axis of a current-carrying coil is: (A) perpendicular to the axis; (B) parallel to the axis; (C) at 45° to the axis; (D) zero. 6. When a coil rotates in a magnetic field, the induced current: (A) continuously changes; (B) remains the same; (C) becomes zero; (D) becomes maximum. 7. In an A.C. generator, increasing the number of turns in the coil: (A) decreases e.m.f.; (B) leaves e.m.f. the same; (C) increases e.m.f.; (D) makes e.m.f. zero. 8. A device in which induced e.m.f. is statically induced is: (A) transformer; (B) A.C. generator; (C) alternator; (D) dynamo. 9. Find mutual-inductance coefficient when magnetic flux changes by 2×10⁻² Wb and current changes by 0.01 A: (A) 2 H; (B) 3 H; (C) 1/2 H; (D) zero. 10. Induced e.m.f. in a coil is proportional to: (A) magnetic flux through the coil; (B) rate of change of magnetic flux through the coil; (C) coil area; (D) product of flux and area. 11. In a coil current changes from 2 to 4 A in 0.05 s. If average induced e.m.f. is 8 V, self-inductance is: (A) 0.2 H; (B) 0.1 H; (C) 0.8 H; (D) 0.04 H. 12. Which quantity remains constant in a step-up transformer? (A) current; (B) voltage; (C) power; (D) heat. 13. A step-up transformer has transformation ratio 3:2. What is secondary voltage if primary voltage is 30 V? (A) 45 V; (B) 15 V; (C) 90 V; (D) 300 V. 14. Eddy current is produced when: (A) a metal is kept in a varying magnetic field; (B) a metal is kept in a steady magnetic field; (C) a circular coil is placed in a steady magnetic field; (D) current is passed through a circular coil.

CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS — 1. What factors limit the size of the back e.m.f.? 2. Why does back e.m.f. tend to decrease as the rate of doing work increases? 3. In Faraday’s experiments, what is the advantage of using coils with many turns? 4. Show that ε = −ΔΦ/Δt is dimensionally correct. 5. Give the formulae for flux linkage in terms of angular orientation. 6. How does an electromagnetic brake work? 7. How can eddy currents be minimized in a transformer? 8. How is electromagnetic induction used in cooktops in electric ranges?

exercises.title: Conceptual questions 9–10, comprehensive questions and numerical problems 1–9
exercises.questions:
CONCEPTUAL QUESTIONS (continued) — 9. What is meant by the term back e.m.f. in operation of an electric motor? 10. Why is it advantageous for the armature to rotate in a radial magnetic field rather than a uniform field? TRANSFORMER CORE: (a) Which material would you prefer: iron, solid soft iron, laminated soft iron or aluminium? (b) Why is this material used?

COMPREHENSIVE QUESTIONS — 1. Describe electromagnetic induction with simple experiments; explain factors affecting magnitude and direction of induced e.m.f. 2. State Faraday’s law; explain statically and dynamically induced e.m.f. with experiments. 3. Describe Lenz’s law and show that it manifests conservation of energy. 4. Explain mutual induction; define its coefficient and unit. 5. Explain self-induction; define its coefficient and unit. 6. Explain motional e.m.f. and show ε = Bℓv. 7. What is a D.C. generator? Explain how an alternating e.m.f. is generated by a loop of wire rotating in a magnetic field. 8. What is an A.C. motor? Explain its construction and operation. 9. What is a transformer? Give its principle and mathematical relationship; explain why a laminated iron core is used instead of a solid core. 10. Explain back e.m.f. in an electric motor.

NUMERICAL PROBLEMS — 1. A wheel has 12 metal spokes, each 0.6 m long, and rotates at 180 rpm in a plane normal to Earth’s magnetic field. If B = 0.6 G, find induced e.m.f. between axle and rim. Printed answer: 2.035 × 10⁻⁴ V. 2. A 1000-turn circuit encloses a magnetic circuit of cross-section 20 cm². At 4 A, B = 1 Wb m⁻²; at 9 A, B = 1.4 Wb m⁻². Find mean inductance between these current limits and e.m.f. if current falls from 9 A to 4 A in 0.05 s. Printed answers: 0.16 H, 16 V. 3. A 100 Ω coil with 100 turns is in a 1 mWb field; a 400 Ω galvanometer is connected in series. Find average e.m.f. and current if the coil moves in 0.1 s from the given field to 0.2 mWb. Printed answer: 1.6 mA. 4. A horizontal east–west wire 10 m long falls at 5.0 m s⁻¹ perpendicular to the horizontal component of Earth’s field, 0.30 × 10⁻⁴ Wb m⁻². Find (a) instantaneous e.m.f., (b) direction, and (c) which end has higher potential. Printed answer: 1.5 × 10⁻³ V.

5. Current in a circuit falls from 5.0 A to 0 A in 0.1 s. If average induced e.m.f. is 200 V, estimate self-inductance. Printed answer: 4 H. 6. A long solenoid has 15 turns per cm. A small loop of area 2.0 cm² is inside, normal to its axis. Solenoid current changes steadily from 2.0 A to 4.0 A in 0.1 s. Find induced e.m.f. in the loop. Printed answer: 7.54 × 10⁻⁶ V. 7. A rectangular loop of sides 8 cm and 2 cm, with a small cut, moves out of a uniform 0.3 T magnetic field normal to the loop at 1 cm s⁻¹. Find e.m.f. and duration when velocity is normal to (a) the longer side, (b) the shorter side. Printed answers: 2.4 × 10⁻⁴ V, 2 s; 0.6 × 10⁻⁴ V, 8 s. 8. A 90 mm wire moves upward at 35 m s⁻¹ between magnet poles. B = 80 mT to the right and wire resistance is 5.00 mΩ. Find induced-current magnitude and direction. Printed answer: 50.4 A. 9. Adjacent coils have mutual inductance 1.5 H. Current in one changes from 0 to 20 A in 0.5 s. Find change of flux linkage with the other coil. Printed answer: 30 Wb.
